title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
abstract: arXiv:2611.29888v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution). We provide a normative second-order Langevin sampling framework wherein spike-frequency adaptation drives spatial exploration at the cost of speed, and momentum via dendritic input differentiation drives temporal compression. translated_title: 噪声循环神经网络中的二阶动力学在海马回放中产生探索与时间压缩
translated_abstract: 生物神经网络（如海马体）能够在内部产生类似于刺激驱动活动的“回放”现象。近期的回放计算模型使用了经过路径积分训练的噪声循环神经网络（RNN），这些网络中的回放被描述为朗之万采样过程，但仅凭这一理论无法解释真实生物回放中观察到的环境探索和时间压缩现象。为了弥补这一差距，我们重新审视了噪声RNN的自发活动（“回放”），将其视为逐时间步的朗之万采样，从一个类似真实生活经历的时间序列分布中进行采样（不同于以往将采样定义为对静态分布进行蒙特卡洛推断的研究）。我们提出了一个规范的二阶朗之万采样框架，其中尖峰频率适应以牺牲速度为代价驱动空间探索，而通过树突输入微分产生的动量则驱动时间压缩。我们通过数值方法验证了我们的（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一个规范的二阶朗之万采样框架，证明噪声RNN中尖峰频率适应驱动空间探索、树突输入微分产生的动量驱动时间压缩，从而成功解释了真实生物回放中的探索行为和时间压缩两大特征。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a normative second-order Langevin sampling framework showing that spike-frequency adaptation drives spatial exploration while dendritic-input-differentiation momentum drives temporal compression, explaining the exploration and temporal compression observed in biological replay.
